sources.title: Structured interview note containing the binary-tree Path Sum prompt
Tagged repository question record mapping Path Sum to LeetCode 112
LeetCode 112 Path Sum official problem page
Deterministic Java validation against independent root-to-leaf sum enumeration

claims.text: The recovered interview note names only Path Sum, while the tagged repository record maps this question to LeetCode 112; the candidate makes that mapping explicit instead of silently conflating Path Sum variants.
Under LeetCode 112 semantics, the result is true only when a root-to-leaf path has values summing to targetSum, and a leaf has no children.
The official 112 constraints allow an empty tree and negative node values; therefore empty input has no root-to-leaf path and monotonic sum pruning is invalid in general.
The exact Java implementation provides recursive residual-sum DFS and an equivalent explicit-stack DFS, and both enforce success only at leaves.

The deterministic fixture compares both implementations with a structurally different BFS enumeration of all root-to-leaf path sums on 3000 fixed-seed random trees and separately verifies a 5000-node deep chain with the iterative implementation.
Both implementations visit each reachable tree node at most once; recursive state occupies O(h) call-stack space and iterative state occupies O(h) explicit-stack space in the worst case.

checks: root-to-leaf leaf-only contract on fixed examples
3000 fixed-seed trees match independent BFS path-sum enumeration
5000-node deep chain succeeds with explicit-stack implementation

boundary_tests.expected: false because no root-to-leaf path exists

boundary_tests.case: internal prefix equals target but node is not a leaf
boundary_tests.expected: false because LeetCode 112 requires the path to end at a leaf
matching negative sum is accepted without monotonic pruning
recursive and iterative results equal independent BFS root-to-leaf sum enumeration
iterative implementation finds the leaf-only sum without relying on JVM recursion depth

findings: The candidate preserves the source boundary: the interview note itself says only Path Sum, and the LeetCode 112 contract is adopted because the repository tagged record explicitly supplies that mapping.
The leaf-only success condition is stated before the implementation and covered by a non-leaf-prefix regression case.
Negative input values are handled without an invalid monotonic pruning assumption.
The randomized oracle enumerates completed root-to-leaf sums with BFS rather than reproducing the residual-sum recursion.
The iterative variant covers the deep-tree operational boundary without claiming JVM recursion depth is guaranteed by the algorithmic contract.
Path Sum II and Path Sum III are distinguished as different contracts rather than silently mixed into the answer.
No production experience or project metrics are fabricated.
Required human approval remains a separate promotion gate.
